subject: Post-call: FinPay discovery + competitive TCO model
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Chen <elaine.chen@finpay.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next tests (FinPay)

Thanks again for taking time today, Elaine — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of needs (from call)
- Real-time fraud detection enrichment (low single-digit-second latency target for lookups)
- High throughput nightly batch scoring for 1B events/day
- Strong auditability and control for PII & retention policies

Competitive / cost context we discussed
- You mentioned you benchmarked Bedrock/Vertex/OpenAI for both costs and dev velocity.
- Key question: unit economics on high-throughput scoring (per-1M tokens) + impact of batching and cache hit rates on TCO.

What we'll deliver next:
1) A short TCO model comparing Redwood Dedicated vs Bedrock + OpenAI (per-1M tokens, expected throughput, and cost sensitivity to cache hit rate). I attached a first-pass spreadsheet (redwood-finpay-tco-v1.xlsx).
2) A recommended test matrix: 
   - Latency-sensitive test: 95th pct latency at 1 replica with small batch sizes (simulate live API).
   - Throughput test: 100k concurrent tokens/sec with batching + KV cache enabled.
   - Cache-effectiveness test: run 1k representative prompts to estimate prefix cache hit rate and reuse.
3) Proposed timeline: run tests next week (Mon/Tue) and share results by Wed.

Next steps for you: please share the procurement contact (cc'd here if possible) and a sample prompt set we can use for cache testing.

Attachments: redwood-finpay-tco-v1.xlsx (first-pass numbers)

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1-415-555-0172

Thanks Aditya — this looks good. Couple quick clarifications before you kick off tests: 

- For the per-1M token numbers, can you show both generation and embedding unit economics? We use embeddings heavily for candidate retrieval.
- For cache hit rate, we can provide a 2k-sample of past queries (anonymized). Is that sufficient?
- Procurement: forwarding procurement lead (procurement@finpay.com) — they handle PO/contract.

I can confirm the team is available next Tue (June 30) for the live test window.

Elaine Chen
Head of Data Platform, FinPay
elaine.chen@finpay.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: FinPay recap — need updated TCO + test config

Folks — forwarding FinPay's clarifying questions. Key asks: 
- Show both generation and embedding per-1M token/unit TCO (with and without batching/caching).
- Provide clear assumptions: model family, QPS, average prompt length, cache hit rate scenarios (10/30/60%).
- Confirm availability to run test on Tue 2026-06-30 (they asked for Tue, but their timezone is PDT).

From my first-pass in the spreadsheet: Redwood hosted quantized model (gptx-q4) baseline: 
- Generation: $9 / 1M tokens (no cache, small batches)
- Embeddings: $4 / 1M embedding units
- With batching (batch=32) and KV/prefix cache 40% hit: effective generation cost drops to ~$5.5 / 1M tokens
- Hyperscaler examples (public list prices, w/o batching effects): Bedrock ~ $18 / 1M gen, OpenAI ~ $16 / 1M gen (these are illustrative; need to normalize for model size & latency SLO)

Action items for Marcus / Monica:
- Marcus: please update the attached spreadsheet with a row for Dedicated vs Hosted, and simulate 3 cache hit scenarios (10/30/60%). Call out assumptions (model, tokenization overhead).
- Monica: coordinate infra to schedule a Dedicated test instance for 6/30 and prepare monitoring hooks (token counts, 95th latency, and cache hit telemetry).

I put procurement contact in cc on the external thread; once we have test results and a short TCO note, we can share an initial commercial estimate to procurement for PO planning.

Thanks — A
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: FinPay recap — need updated TCO + test config

Adding the numbers now. A couple of things I'll model explicitly: 
- Tokenization overhead: we assume 1.1x tokens per labeled unit (FinPay uses long JSON inputs).
- Batching sensitivity: model latency increases beyond batch=64 on the Dedicated config; we'll show latency vs batch-size tradeoff.
- Cost amortization for idle nodes (Dedicated reserved) — include reserved vs burst pricing.

Preliminary delta vs hyperscalers: with caching + aggressive batching Redwood Dedicated can be ~30-45% lower TCO for long-running scoring workloads vs public endpoints. I'll attach v2 of the spreadsheet when done.

Marcus

Redwood Inference
